## Goals (impact map)

The vision has three success criteria. Each one has a different actor or a different impact, so each
becomes its own goal.

### Goal 1: Owners offer their unused garden space
- **Actor:** a garden owner in the town with space they do not use
- **Impact:** publishes a plot offer, where today they would rely on word of mouth or leave the space idle
- **Success metric (success criterion 1):** a first-time owner who starts signed out on the landing page publishes a plot with its size and access times in under 5:00, measured by a timed walkthrough.

### Goal 2: Growers on the waiting list find and request a plot nearby
- **Actor:** a person on the town's allotment waiting list who wants to grow vegetables
- **Impact:** finds and requests a plot within 1 km, where today they wait about three years
- **Success metric (success criterion 2):** a first-time grower who starts signed out on the landing page sends a request for an open plot within 1 km in under 5:00, measured by a timed walkthrough.

### Goal 3: Owners answer requests and the plots become shared
- **Actor:** the garden owner, who decides; the grower receives the outcome
- **Impact:** owners answer requests, so that a request becomes a shared plot
- **Success metric (success criterion 3):** 50 distinct plots reach "shared" (an accepted request) within six months of launch.

(the owner offers, the grower finds and requests, the owner accepts, both sides get the hand-over

### Stub 1: `garden-share-mvp.md` (block to insert)

#### Goals covered
All three goals (actors, impacts and metrics as in the goals section above). This stub delivers the
thinnest version of all three success criteria end to end.

#### Activities and stories

##### Goal 1, Activity 1.1 Join
- [ ] **1.1.1 [MVP] Create an account and sign back in.** As a garden owner, I want to create an account with my email address and sign back in later, so that my plot offer and the requests for it stay tied to me.
  - Acceptance: a new email address plus a credential creates an account and leaves the person signed in. An email address that already has an account is refused with "This email already has an account, sign in instead." A signed-out person who follows a link to a page that needs an account (for example the request link in an email) is asked to sign in and then lands on that page. In a timed walkthrough, a first-time user creates an account in under 60 seconds.
  - The sign-in mechanism (password or emailed sign-in link) is left to the Product Owner.

##### Goal 1, Activity 1.2 Describe the plot
- [ ] **1.2.1 [MVP] Offer a plot with address, size and access times.** As a garden owner, I want to offer a plot by giving its address, its size in square metres and its weekly access times, so that growers nearby can find it.
  - Acceptance: address, size (whole square metres, 1 to 5,000) and at least one weekly access window (day of the week, from-time, to-time, with the to-time after the from-time) are required. The address is turned into a map location, and the listing is saved as "open" and shown to the owner as soon as it is submitted. A missing size, a missing access window or a to-time before its from-time gives an error that names the field, and nothing is saved. Example: "Lindenlaan 12, 25 m², Sat 09:00–13:00, Wed 18:00–20:00" gives an open listing that shows 25 m² and both windows. In a timed walkthrough, a first-time owner starting signed out on the landing page has a published listing in under 5:00, including 1.1.1 (success criterion 1).
  - This story carries the geocoding provider setup.

##### Goal 1, Activity 1.3 Keep the offer current
- [ ] **1.3.1 [MVP] See my plots and their status.** As a garden owner, I want a page that lists my plots with their status, so that I know where each offer stands.
  - Acceptance: the page shows every plot of the signed-in owner and no one else's, each with its stored status (open, shared or withdrawn), street name and size. An owner with no plots sees a link to offer one.

##### Goal 2, Activity 2.1 Search nearby
- [ ] **2.1.1 [MVP] Search open plots within 1 km.** As a grower, I want to enter my address and see the open plots within one kilometre, nearest first, with size, access times and distance, so that I can find a plot I can reach easily.
  - Acceptance: no account is needed. With open plots 0.4 km, 0.9 km and 1.2 km (straight line) from the entered address, the results show the 0.4 km plot, then the 0.9 km plot, and the 1.2 km plot does not appear. Shared and withdrawn plots never appear. Each result shows its size, its access windows, its distance rounded to 0.1 km and its street name without the house number. When no plot is open within 1 km, the page says "No open plots within 1 km of this address" instead of showing an empty list. An address that cannot be located gives an error asking the grower to check it.

##### Goal 2, Activity 2.2 Request a plot
- [ ] **2.2.1 [MVP] Join as a grower on the waiting list.** As a grower on the town's allotment waiting list, I want to create an account partway through requesting a plot and state that I am on the waiting list, so that I can request without losing my place in the search.
  - Acceptance: starting a request while signed out offers sign-up or sign-in and then returns to the same plot. Grower sign-up cannot be submitted until "I am on the town's allotment waiting list" is ticked. It uses the account mechanism from 1.1.1, so one account can both offer and request.
- [ ] **2.2.2 [MVP] Request a plot with a message.** As a grower, I want to open a plot's details and send its owner a request with a short message, so that the owner knows I want to grow there and why.
  - Acceptance: the plot detail page shows the size, access windows, distance and street name, and never the house number or the owner's contact details. A message of 1 to 1,000 characters is required. Sending creates a pending request linked to the plot and the grower, and the grower sees "Request sent". A second request for the same plot by the same grower while one is pending is refused with "You already have a pending request for this plot." Owners cannot request their own plot. In a timed walkthrough, a first-time grower starting signed out on the landing page sends a request for a plot within 1 km in under 5:00, including 2.2.1 (success criterion 2).

##### Goal 2, Activity 2.3 Follow up
- [ ] **2.3.1 [MVP] See my requests and their status.** As a grower, I want a page that lists my requests with their status, so that I know where I stand.
  - Acceptance: the page lists every request of the signed-in grower, newest first, with the plot's street name, the date sent and the stored status (pending, accepted or declined). It shows no one else's requests.

##### Goal 3, Activity 3.1 Learn about requests
- [ ] **3.1.1 [MVP] Owner is emailed about a new request.** As a garden owner, I want an email when a grower requests my plot, so that I can respond without checking the site.
  - Acceptance: within 5 minutes of the request, the owner gets an email with the plot's street name, the grower's first name, the message and a link to the request. The email holds no grower email address or phone number.
  - This is the first email in the system, so the story carries the email-sending setup.
- [ ] **3.1.2 [MVP] See the requests for my plots.** As a garden owner, I want to see the pending requests for each of my plots, with each grower's first name, message, waiting-list statement and date, so that I can choose whom to accept.
  - Acceptance: the owner sees only requests on plots they own. A direct link to another owner's request returns "not found". The "My plots" page shows the number of pending requests for each plot.

##### Goal 3, Activity 3.2 Decide
- [ ] **3.2.1 [MVP] Accept a request.** As a garden owner, I want to accept one request for my plot, so that that grower can start growing there.
  - Acceptance: the request becomes accepted, the plot becomes shared, and the plot disappears from search at once. Accepting works only on a pending request for an open plot the owner owns. A second accept on a plot that is already shared is refused with "This plot is already shared." The plot now counts once toward the 50 shared plots of success criterion 3.

##### Goal 3, Activity 3.3 Start sharing
- [ ] **3.3.1 [MVP] Hand-over details to both sides.** As a grower whose request was accepted, I want an email and an entry on my requests page with the owner's name, the owner's email address, the plot's full address and its access times, so that we can arrange the first visit.
  - Acceptance: the email arrives within 5 minutes of acceptance with those fields. The owner's "My plots" page shows the grower's name and email address for the shared plot. Before acceptance, neither side can see the other's contact details or the house number (checked on the pages from 2.2.2 and 3.1.2).

### Stub 2: `garden-share-offer-a-plot.md` (block to insert)

#### Goal
Goal 1, owners offer their unused garden space (actor, impact and metric in the goals section).
These are the owner-side stories outside the walking skeleton.

#### Activities and stories

##### Activity 1.1 Join
- [ ] **1.1.2 Recover access by email.** As an owner or grower who cannot sign in, I want to regain access through my email address, so that I don't lose my plots or requests.
  - Acceptance: a recovery email reaches the account's address within 5 minutes. Its link works once and expires after 1 hour. An unknown email address gets the same neutral on-screen message as a known one, so the form cannot be used to find out who has an account.

##### Activity 1.2 Describe the plot
- [ ] **1.2.2 Describe growing conditions.** As a garden owner, I want to add optional details (sunlight, a water tap nearby, soil, and what may or may not be grown), so that growers can judge whether the plot suits them before they request it.
  - Acceptance: every detail is optional, and a listing publishes without any of them, so the 5-minute clock in success criterion 1 is not affected. Details that are given appear on the plot detail page. The free text is at most 500 characters.
- [ ] **1.2.3 Add photos.** As a garden owner, I want to add up to 4 photos of the plot, so that growers can see what they would get.
  - Acceptance: JPEG or PNG, up to 10 MB each, at most 4 per plot. The photos appear on the plot detail page, and the first one appears as a thumbnail in search results. Location metadata (EXIF GPS) is removed on upload, because it would reveal the exact address that stays hidden until acceptance.
- [ ] **1.2.4 Place the plot on a map when the address isn't found.** As a garden owner whose address is not recognised, I want to set the plot's location on a map myself, so that I can still offer it.
  - Acceptance: when the address cannot be located, the owner sees a map of the town and drops a pin. The listing is saved with the pin's location and appears in distance searches the same way as a geocoded plot.

##### Activity 1.3 Keep the offer current
- [ ] **1.3.2 Edit an open plot.** As a garden owner, I want to change the size, access times, details or location of my open plot, so that the listing stays accurate.
  - Acceptance: the same validation as 1.2.1 applies. Changes appear in search and on the detail page at once. Editing is offered for open plots only.
- [ ] **1.3.3 Withdraw or republish a plot.** As a garden owner, I want to withdraw an open plot and republish it later, so that I stop receiving requests while the space is not available.
  - Acceptance: a withdrawn plot disappears from search at once. Its pending requests become declined, and each of those growers gets an email saying the plot was withdrawn. Republishing sets the plot back to open, and it appears in search again.

- [ ] **2.1.2 Filter by size and access day.** As a grower, I want to filter results by minimum size and by access day, so that I only see plots that fit my needs and my week.
  - Acceptance: a minimum of 20 m² hides a 15 m² plot. The day "Saturday" shows only plots that have a Saturday window. Filters combine (all must match), and clearing them restores the full list.

- [ ] **2.1.4 Widen the radius.** As a grower with no open plot within 1 km, I want to widen the search to 2 or 3 km, so that I still see plots I might take.
  - Acceptance: the radius choices are 1, 2 and 3 km, and every new search starts at 1 km. Results beyond 1 km are clearly labelled with their distance.
- [ ] **2.1.5 Get an email when a plot opens nearby.** As a grower who found nothing suitable, I want an email when a plot opens within 1 km of my address, so that I don't have to keep checking.
  - Acceptance: this needs an account and one saved address per grower. An email arrives within 15 minutes of a plot being published or reopened within 1 km, with at most one email per plot. Every alert has an unsubscribe link that works in one click.

- [ ] **2.3.2 Withdraw a pending request.** As a grower, I want to withdraw a pending request, so that the owner doesn't accept a plot I no longer want.

## Decisions Taken Under Ambiguity

Each of these was taken so the work could continue without blocking. All of them await the owner's
review.

1. **Slicing: an MVP stub plus three goal stubs, not one stub per goal.** The three goals form one
   two-sided journey. With one stub per goal, the stubs form a strict chain (offer → request →
   answer) and no single stub completes a share. With the MVP stub carrying the whole thinnest
   journey, stubs 2 to 4 depend only on it and not on each other. The alternative (3 stubs, one per
   goal, chained) can be made with `mergeStubs` / `createStub`.
2. **Story-level chain depth of 6 inside stub 1 accepted** (checklist item 7). It is inherent to the
   journey, and flattening it would create a horizontal slice.
3. **No delivery phases assigned.** The method's grouping into walking skeleton, flesh out and
   polish is not applied, because by standing instruction the owner alone decides what is built
   and when. "[MVP]" marks the dependency root only.
4. **"Shared plot" means a plot with an accepted request.** Success criterion 3 counts distinct
   plots, so a plot reopened and shared again counts once.
5. **The five-minute clocks start signed out on the landing page and include creating an account
   for a first-time user**, ending at the published listing (criterion 1) or the sent request
   (criterion 2). This is the stricter reading. Measurement: a timed walkthrough with five
   first-time testers, each of whom must finish in under 5:00.
6. **Distance is the straight line** from the grower's entered address to the plot's map location.
   Walking distance would need a routing service.
7. **Privacy:** before acceptance, search and detail pages show the distance and street name only,
   with no house number and no contact details. Photos have their location metadata removed. Map
   markers are snapped to about 100 m.
8. **Waiting-list membership is self-declared** (a required tickbox) and not checked against the
   town's list.
9. **Searching needs no account; requesting does.** This keeps the five-minute grower clock
   reachable.
10. **One plot goes to one grower.** An owner sharing with two growers lists two plots.
11. **One account type.** The same account can offer and request.
12. **Access times are structured weekly windows** (day of the week, from and to), so that the
    filter by day in 2.1.2 is possible.
13. **"Mobile app" out of scope is read as a native app.** The web app must work in a phone browser.
    Notifications go by email.
14. **The numbers chosen are:** plot size 1 to 5,000 m²; message 1 to 1,000 characters; request
    expiry after 14 days; radius choices of 1, 2 and 3 km; up to 4 photos of 10 MB each; alert
    within 15 minutes.
15. **Story 3.3.2, reopening a plot after a share ends, is included although the vision's scope
    neither lists nor excludes it.** Without it, an owner whose grower leaves would have to create
    a duplicate listing. It is a separate story, so it can be dropped.
16. **Story 2.1.5, the new-plot alert, is included** because a one-town marketplace starts sparse,
    and growers who find nothing on day one would otherwise not come back. That matters directly for
    the target of 50 shared plots.
17. **This proposal is written to `plans/decompositions/garden-share.md`**, a new file outside
    `plans/functional/` and `plans/vision/`, so that no tool mistakes it for a stub or a vision. The
    stubs themselves are left to the library.
